Researchers Identify Mutation-Specific Metabolic Vulnerabilities in Liver Cancer
item.description:
Researchers at Rockefeller University have identified distinct metabolic vulnerabilities in liver cancer cells, revealing how specific genetic mutations influence the nutrients and cellular processes tumors depend on to survive. The findings could contribute to the development of more personalized cancer treatments.
The research, conducted by Kıvanç Birsoy and his team, including research associate Gokhan Unlu, focuses on cancer metabolism: the processes through which cancer cells obtain and use nutrients to generate energy and support their growth. Because cancer cells often become unusually dependent on particular metabolic pathways, disrupting these processes could provide new ways to fight tumors.
One of the main challenges in studying cancer metabolism is that metabolic activity changes rapidly and tumors contain a mixture of cancer cells, healthy cells, and immune cells. These factors make it difficult to identify the specific metabolic characteristics of cancer cells. To addre

item.title: Iowa's Military Explosives Disposal and Governor Reynolds's Political Ties to Israel
item.description:
The article examines two seemingly unrelated developments in Iowa: the Army's detonation of nearly five tons of lead azide at a military facility and Governor Kim Reynolds's political and economic relationship with Israel. It questions the timing of the military operation, its potential environmental consequences, and the governor's priorities.
According to the article, the Army carried out the explosives disposal on the Wednesday before Thanksgiving 2026, citing favorable weather conditions and concerns that colder temperatures could increase the risk of an uncontrolled explosion. Major General Eric Shirley reportedly told a federal court that prevailing winds would carry the resulting plume away from population centers and major bodies of water. The Agriculture Department estimated that approximately 350 farms could be affected.

item.title: A Father Learns to Listen More and Speak Less During a Visit With His Son
item.description:
This Modern Love essay, written by a 67-year-old father, explores his effort to build a closer relationship with his adult son through phone calls and a visit in New York. The writer explains that he and his son never developed an easy habit of casual conversation, particularly by phone. By the time his son left home for graduate school, the father realized that closeness would not develop naturally unless he made a deliberate effort to create it.
The essay traces the distance between father and son to the son’s early infancy. Born with a coronary fistula, the boy needed heart surgery when he was only seven weeks old. During the period before surgery and throughout recovery, doctors prevented breastfeeding until he was well. When breastfeeding resumed, the writer says his son formed a profound bond with his mother that he felt outside of. He acknowledges that many fathers miss some of the intimacy created through breastfeeding, and that caring for the couple’s daughter while his son w

item.title: U.S. Army Completes Controlled Detonation of 68 Drums of Explosive Material in Iowa
item.description:
The U.S. Army announced the successful controlled detonation of 68 drums of unstable explosive material at a munitions facility in Iowa on Wednesday. The operation followed approximately 10 days of public concern, evacuations, legal disputes, and safety measures aimed at minimizing the environmental and health risks associated with potentially toxic lead dust.
The material, identified as degraded lead azide, is a highly reactive compound used in the manufacture of munitions. On November 15, the Army announced that it intended to destroy the material through a controlled explosion after ruling out alternative disposal methods. A previously planned chemical neutralization process involving a remediation company was also canceled.
To reduce the risks associated with the detonation, military personnel implemented extensive protective measures around the storage structures. According to documents reviewed by The Washington Post, the operation involved earth-covered bunkers surrounded by p

item.title: How Major Life Changes and Personal Crises Can Affect Longstanding Friendships
item.description:
In this installment of the advice column “Asking Eric,” R. Eric Thomas addresses a question about how major life changes and personal crises can affect longstanding friendships.
The letter comes from someone who had maintained a close friendship with another person for many years. Their relationship developed through participation in the same 12-step program, where they regularly attended a weekly meeting. Over time, their connection extended beyond those gatherings. They established a routine of meeting for coffee before their weekly meetings and occasionally traveled together on weekends to visit nearby destinations, shop, or attend theatrical performances in a larger city.
Although the two friends came from different backgrounds and had different childhood experiences, they developed a meaningful bond despite those differences. The writer believed the friendship was strong and enduring, based on their shared activities, regular contact, and years of companionship.
However, the re

item.title: Dubai Businessman Prepares New Bid to Rescue Poundland After Collapse
item.description:
Dubai-based businessman Idris Mohammed is preparing a renewed bid to acquire British discount retailer Poundland after the company entered administration, threatening more than 10,000 jobs. Mohammed, owner of Premier Quality Foods, intends to approach AlixPartners, the retailer's appointed administrator, in an effort to purchase the business and preserve as much of its operations as possible.
Mohammed had previously been among four potential buyers negotiating with Poundland's owner, US investment firm Gordon Brothers, before the retailer's collapse. He said his team had developed a six-month recovery plan focused on restoring profitability by securing better purchasing prices for branded products, reducing inventory losses, improving staffing schedules, and cutting distribution and head-office expenses.
According to Mohammed, the main obstacle to completing an earlier acquisition was securing sufficient financing to cover Poundland's historical liabilities while maintaining enough w

item.title: A Virginia Butcher Developed Alpha-Gal Syndrome After a Tick Bite
item.description:
This New York Times article tells the story of Derek Luhowiak, a Virginia butcher and chef whose life changed after he developed symptoms following a tick bite. One summer morning, Luhowiak woke with an itchy, hard red bump on the underside of his left foot. He initially assumed it was a spider bite, but a similar bump soon appeared on his right foot. A rash then spread across his body, his hands swelled, and his tongue began to swell, leaving him concerned that he might be experiencing anaphylactic shock.
After seeing a doctor, he received a corticosteroid to reduce inflammation, but the underlying cause was not immediately identified. His symptoms continued, including persistent fatigue and stress. The situation became more serious one night when his esophagus constricted and he went to the emergency room. The article’s title and URL indicate that the condition involved was alpha-gal syndrome, an allergy associated with tick bites that can cause reactions to red meat and other mamma

item.title: Amazon Workers Plan Worldwide Strikes and Protests Over Pay and Working Conditions
item.description:
Amazon employees in more than 20 countries are preparing to stage strikes, demonstrations, and rallies during the company's busiest shopping weekend of the year. The coordinated action will take place around Black Friday and continue through Cyber Monday, targeting warehouses, delivery stations, and corporate offices.
The international campaign, organized by UNI Global Union and Progressive International under the banner Make Amazon Pay, aims to pressure the retail giant to negotiate with trade unions, improve employee compensation, and respect workers' rights to organize. Participants have raised concerns about inadequate wages, excessive workplace monitoring, and allegedly oppressive working conditions.
In Germany, employees at 11 Amazon locations are scheduled to strike. The United Services Trade Union is demanding recognition of collective bargaining agreements covering the retail sector, as well as agreements guaranteeing healthier working conditions. The union has criticized re

item.title: 46 Holiday Gift Ideas Featuring Design, Home Goods, Games, and Outdoor Accessories
item.description:
Moss & Fog presents its 2026 holiday gift guide, featuring 46 carefully selected products from its own shop and independent brands and retailers. Organized into eight themed sections, the collection brings together practical items, distinctive design objects, entertaining games, and thoughtful gifts for different interests and budgets.
The desk section includes a wireless lamp that doubles as a phone charger, colorful pens, notebooks, an instant camera, a fountain pen, and a LEGO interpretation of Vincent van Gogh's The Starry Night. For gift wrapping and stationery enthusiasts, the selection features illustrated wrapping paper books, Bauhaus-inspired designs, handcrafted greeting cards, and decorative washi tape.
The kitchen collection focuses on durable cookware and food treats. Highlights include a Made In carbon steel frying pan, a classic Lodge cast-iron skillet, a Bialetti Moka Express coffee maker, reusable beeswax food wraps, and two varieties of dark chocolate from Portland-

item.title: Congress Nears Deal on Legislation to Restrict Chinese-Made Connected Cars
item.description: Congress appears increasingly likely to pass bipartisan legislation before the end of the year that would restrict the sale of vehicles connected to China and Russia. The Connected Vehicle Security Act, sponsored by Republican Senator Bernie Moreno of Ohio and Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, would prohibit U.S. sales of cars containing components from countries considered adversaries. Its supporters hope to advance it through the Senate by voice vote in December and to move it quickly through the House during the lame-duck session. The bill has gained momentum after negotiations with major automakers and advocacy groups addressed concerns about how it would define a Chinese vehicle. The original proposal would have barred cars made by companies with more than 15 percent Chinese ownership, a standard that could have affected Mercedes-Benz and Volvo, which have substantial Chinese investment. item.title: Eight Black Friday Deals on Roku, Keurig, Nintendo and Kids' Headphones
item.description:
Black Friday 2026 brings discounts on a variety of electronics, entertainment devices, coffee makers, and children's accessories. Fox News contributor Limor Suss highlights eight deals featured on the Shopping with Friends program, with prices starting at approximately $14.
Among the featured offers is the Roku 65-inch Pro Series Smart TV, reduced from $1,200 to approximately $800, representing a 33% discount. The television offers high-definition picture quality, Bluetooth connectivity, voice controls, backlit remote buttons, and a remote finder feature.
Coffee enthusiasts can save on two Keurig models. The K-Supreme Gen 2 single-serve coffee maker is available for $110, down from $170. It offers adjustable brewing strength and temperature, along with four cup sizes ranging from 6 to 12 ounces. Meanwhile, the compact K-Mini Mate Plus costs $63, compared with its original $110 price. item.title: Researchers Seek Mathematical Safeguards to Keep Advanced AI Aligned With Human Goals
item.description:
This New York Times Magazine article follows Mike Winer, a 30-year-old researcher in Berkeley, California, who is working on a mathematical approach to keeping artificial intelligence aligned with human intentions. Winer and a small group of mathematicians and researchers are trying to develop methods that could ensure advanced AI systems pursue goals people actually want, before the technology becomes too powerful or complex to control. The article presents this as one of the most consequential problems in AI safety: designing safeguards that remain reliable as AI capabilities expand.
Winer describes the work as the final major mathematical challenge of his career. He and colleagues, including statistics postdoctoral researcher Reese Pathak, meet to examine equations, test ideas, and confront the uncertainty surrounding how quickly AI is improving. item.title: Hamilton and Leclerc Seek to Resolve Tensions After Series of Ferrari Collisions
item.description:
Lewis Hamilton has acknowledged that Ferrari is going through a particularly difficult period following a series of on-track incidents involving him and teammate Charles Leclerc. Both drivers held discussions with team principal Frederic Vasseur upon arriving at the Qatar Grand Prix on Thursday, aiming to address the tensions created by their latest collision at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
Vasseur previously described the Las Vegas incident as completely unacceptable. Leclerc received a 10-second penalty after making contact with Hamilton and sending him into a spin. Hamilton had also received a 10-second penalty earlier in the race for gaining an advantage by cutting the track while battling McLaren's Lando Norris.
The confrontation in Las Vegas was the second significant incident between the Ferrari teammates in just three races. Their first-lap battle at the Mexican Grand Prix last month compromised Ferrari's chances of securing a one-two finish, allowing Red Bull's Max Verstappen t

item.title: Research Links Online True Crime Communities to a Growing Number of Violent Attacks
item.description:
A new report from the Network Contagion Research Institute (NCRI) warns that a growing online community fascinated by mass shooters and serial killers is increasingly associated with real-world violence. Known as the True Crime Community (TCC), this network consists largely of young people who glorify perpetrators of mass killings, imitate their behavior, and share content celebrating their attacks.
According to data shared with WIRED, the number of attacks and attempted attacks linked to the community increased from 13 in 2024 to 30 by mid-October 2026, representing a rise of more than 200 percent. The incidents have also spread internationally, with cases recorded in 13 countries during 2026 and approximately two-thirds occurring outside the United States. Researchers warn that the trend could accelerate further without effective intervention.
The TCC has existed for years, with much of its early activity concentrated on Tumblr. However, after Tumblr introduced a major account ban

item.description: POLITICO’s video report examines California Governor Gavin Newsom’s positioning ahead of the 2028 presidential campaign. item.title: Peter Mandelson Advised to Tone Down Praise of Trump Administration in Draft Speech
item.description:
Former British ambassador to the United States Peter Mandelson was advised to moderate his favorable comments about President Donald Trump's administration in a draft speech, according to documents reported by Politico and The New York Times.
The documents reveal that in August 2025, an unnamed director at Global Counsel, the lobbying and consulting firm co-founded by Mandelson, criticized the tone of his draft speech. In an email, the director said they had suggested changes to reduce what they described as Mandelson's excessive defense of the Trump administration. The director warned that public skepticism toward Trump's government was so widespread that Mandelson risked appearing unconvincing if he seemed overly supportive.

item.title: Critical Authentication Vulnerability Discovered in Tenda RX3 Router Firmware
item.description:
A critical authentication vulnerability has been identified in the Tenda RX3 router running firmware version 16.03.13.11_multi. Tracked as CVE-2026-136553, the security flaw affects the device's password-change endpoint, /goform/fast_setting_wifi_set, where manipulation of the loginPwd parameter can lead to improper authentication.
According to the published security advisory, the vulnerability can be exploited remotely, and a public proof of concept is available. The GitHub advisory reports a critical CVSS v4 score of 9.3, indicating a potentially serious security risk. However, the available information does not establish that every affected router is accessible over the internet or that all exposed devices are necessarily vulnerable to successful attacks.
The underlying problem involves inadequate authentication checks when processing requests to change Wi-Fi credentials. Such operations should require a valid administrative session and verification of the current credentials or a

item.title: Michael Wolff Predicts Divisions Within Trump Family as Congressional Investigations Loom
item.description:
Donald Trump's family could face growing internal divisions as congressional investigations into alleged corruption involving the president and his associates approach, according to political biographer Michael Wolff.
Speaking Thursday on the podcast 'Inside Trump's Head,' hosted by Joanna Coles, Wolff predicted that members of the Trump family would increasingly prioritize their individual interests rather than present a united front when investigations begin. Although several family members may gather at Mar-a-Lago for Thanksgiving, he argued that their public appearance together should not be interpreted as evidence of a coordinated strategy to handle potential legal and political challenges.
Wolff identified corruption as a likely central focus of investigations by Democrats in Congress. He suggested that scrutiny could extend beyond Donald Trump to include his sons, his wife, members of his Cabinet, and other individuals within his political and personal circle.

item.title: SeaWorld's Jump-Roping Toy Soldiers Become an Unexpected Social Media Sensation
item.description:
A group of holiday-themed jump-rope performers at SeaWorld Orlando has unexpectedly become an internet sensation thanks to a series of humorous, AI-generated videos that turn the performers into fictional sports celebrities.
The videos are published by @wejumprope_memes, an account managed by Devin Meek, an Orlando-based professional entertainer who performs as Holidave. Meek has been part of SeaWorld's jump-roping toy soldier troupe for six years and has practiced the sport for approximately two decades. What began as an inside joke intended to entertain his coworkers has attracted millions of views and inspired a growing online fan community.
The videos feature fictional biographies, statistics, and exaggerated achievements for the performers, including their supposed net worth, jumping abilities, and personal characteristics. item.title: Former U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott Dies at 80
item.description:
Strobe Talbott, a former U.S. deputy secretary of state and longtime expert on relations with the Soviet Union and Russia, died Thursday at the age of 80. His son, Devin Talbott, confirmed that he passed away peacefully after a long illness at his home in East Hampton, New York, according to The Associated Press.
Born in Ohio, Talbott began his career in journalism as an intern at Time magazine while studying at Yale University and Oxford University. During his time at Oxford, he shared an apartment with future President Bill Clinton, who later recalled humorously that he was responsible for preparing Talbott's breakfast every morning.
Talbott's expertise in international affairs developed during his 21-year career at Time. He became particularly knowledgeable about U.S.-Soviet relations after being assigned to translate the leaked memoirs of former Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev. He subsequently became a full-time staff member, led the magazine's Washington bureau, and worked as a

item.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Receives Version 1.1.2 Update Fixing Malon's Friend Event
item.description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 has received its first post-launch update, bringing the game to version 1.1.2. Released on November 25, 2026, the update is now rolling out to all players and focuses primarily on fixing a progression issue affecting a specific in-game event.
According to Nintendo's official patch notes, the main fix addresses a bug that prevented some players from progressing through the 'Malon's Friend' event. This issue could interrupt gameplay by preventing players from advancing through the affected section of the adventure. Fortunately, Nintendo has confirmed that players who previously encountered the problem do not need to restart their game or begin a new playthrough. Simply downloading and installing the version 1.1.2 update will allow them to continue progressing through the event.
In addition to this specific correction, Nintendo has addressed several other unspecified issues to provide a smoother overall gameplay experience. The

item.title: Google Patent Proposes Personalized AI-Generated Video Feeds Featuring Users as Main Characters
item.description:
Google has filed a patent for a system called My Channel that could generate personalized video feeds featuring AI-created entertainment and advertisements tailored to individual users. Although the patent was rejected, Google could appeal the decision or submit an amended application, potentially bringing the concept closer to reality.
First identified by Patentlyze, the patent describes a system that would use demographic information, viewing histories, and other personal data to generate prompts for large language models (LLMs). These prompts would then guide AI video-generation tools in producing content based on each user's interests and preferences. The system could also collect contextual information from devices, including IP addresses, GPS locations, and age-related details. Current news, sports results, and social media activity could provide additional material for generating videos.

item.title: Trump Discusses Iran's Military Destruction When Asked About Netanyahu
item.description:
President Donald Trump appeared to confuse a question about Israel with a discussion of Iran during remarks to reporters on Thanksgiving Day, according to a report published by Raw Story on November 26, 2026.
After speaking with U.S. service members deployed overseas, Trump was asked whether he had been in contact with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and how he planned to handle Israel's upcoming leadership changes. Instead of directly addressing the question, Trump began discussing Iran and the damage inflicted on its military during U.S. operations.
Trump said the United States was giving Iran an opportunity to make sensible decisions, then described the country's military capabilities as severely diminished. He claimed that Iran's air force, navy, and air defense systems had been destroyed. He also referred to Iranian nuclear facilities that the United States had previously targeted.

item.title: The Socialist Fraternal Kiss: A Diplomatic Gesture of Cold War Era Communism
item.description: The Socialist Fraternal Kiss, a distinctive greeting practice among communist leaders during the Cold War, has become a recognizable symbol of political solidarity in historical photographs. This tradition, which involved leaders exchanging kisses on the lips or cheeks, originated from older European and religious customs but evolved into a formalized diplomatic ritual. The practice began in the early Soviet era, with photographs from the 1930s showing figures like Valery Chkalov kissing Joseph Stalin, establishing the image of Soviet leaders as paternal figures welcoming national heroes. The gesture carried significant political meaning, especially as the Soviet Union expanded its influence across Eastern Europe. The kiss was used to signal unity between communist states, with variations in the greeting reflecting the state of diplomatic relations. item.title: Cadence Secures $100 Million for AI-Powered Chronic Care Platform Expansion
item.description: Cadence has successfully raised $100 million in Series C funding led by Spark Capital, with additional participation from Thrive Capital, General Catalyst, Coatue, B Capital, Corewell Health Ventures, Memorial Hermann, and Duke Health. The company's AI-powered chronic care platform currently serves over 100,000 patients and reportedly saves Medicare approximately $2.7 million weekly. The funding will be allocated toward expanding partnerships with health systems, developing advanced AI agents, and growing their value-based care initiatives. This significant investment underscores the increasing role of artificial intelligence in transforming chronic disease management and healthcare delivery systems. The platform's ability to reduce costs while improving patient outcomes represents a key development in the healthcare technology sector. item.title: Gordon Ramsay Welcomes First Grandchild as Daughter Holly Announces Birth of Baby Girl Daphne
item.description: Gordon Ramsay, the 60-year-old British celebrity chef, has become a grandfather for the first time following the birth of his granddaughter Daphne June Ramsay-Peaty. His daughter Holly Ramsay-Peaty, who is married to Adam Peaty, shared the joyful news on Instagram on Thursday, just in time for Thanksgiving. In her post, Holly revealed the baby's name and expressed gratitude to medical professionals who assisted during the birth. The newborn, born on November 25, was introduced to the world with a heartfelt caption that included photos of Holly and Adam cradling their infant daughter in the hospital. Gordon Ramsay, who has six children with his wife Tana Ramsay, reacted with excitement in the comments section of his daughter's post, writing, 'Welcome Miss Daphne, congratulations to Adam & Holly wow wow wow.' item.title: Rare 1864 Panoramic Views Capture San Francisco's Mid-19th Century Landscape
item.description: The rare 1864 panoramic photographs taken by American photographer Carleton Watkins provide a remarkable glimpse into San Francisco during a pivotal period in its early development. Created more than a decade after the Gold Rush, these images capture the city's expansion along the hills and waterfront, showcasing a mix of wooden structures, unpaved streets, and the emerging urban landscape. At a time when panoramic photography was a complex technical achievement, these views offer an unusually wide and detailed record of the city before the devastating 1906 earthquake and fire. The photographs, which include views toward Russian Hill, North Beach, Alcatraz Island, Mission Bay, Rincon Point, and Telegraph Hill, stand as invaluable historical documents preserving the mid-19th century appearance of San Francisco with striking clarity and breadth. item.title: Trump's Statement on Military Conflict Duration Sparks Outrage Among Troops
item.description: US President Donald Trump made a controversial statement during Thanksgiving calls to deployed military personnel from Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida, on November 26, 2026. According to the report by Bennito L. Kelty of Raw Story, Trump told the troops that their war would end 'whenever I want it to be.' This remark has generated significant backlash and anger among service members and military observers. The president's comments, made during a routine holiday call, have been widely criticized for undermining military professionalism and the chain of command. Kelty, an award-winning journalist with experience covering border issues and politics, reported on the incident as part of his ongoing coverage of government and military affairs. The statement has raised questions about presidential authority over military operations and the implications for troop morale. item.title: Hunger Games Producer Regrets Splitting Mockingjay Films into Two Parts
item.description: Lionsgate producer Nina Jacobson has expressed regret over splitting the final book of The Hunger Games trilogy, 'Mockingjay,' into two films. Speaking in an interview with Empire, Jacobson acknowledged that while she loves the Mockingjay films, she believes the decision to divide the story into two parts might have been better handled as a single film. This decision followed the trend set by franchises like The Twilight Saga and Harry Potter, which also split their final installments into two movies. Jacobson noted that both she and director Francis Lawrence might reconsider the approach if given the chance to redo the project. The comment comes as Lionsgate prepares to release 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,' a prequel to the original series. Fans have previously criticized the split, feeling it was a strategy to make audiences watch two films instead of one. item.description: The article titled 'Guess who's the turkey this Thanksgiving' by Nick Anderson of Raw Story presents an opinion piece discussing the selection of a turkey for Thanksgiving dinner. The author, a contributor to Raw Story, explores the cultural significance of choosing a turkey for the holiday meal, highlighting how this seemingly simple decision can become a point of contention within families and communities. The piece touches on the various factors that influence turkey selection, including dietary preferences, ethical considerations regarding animal welfare, and the growing trend of plant-based alternatives. Anderson notes that while traditional turkey has long been the centerpiece of Thanksgiving feasts, modern households are increasingly considering alternatives due to health concerns, environmental impact, and ethical reasons. item.title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade Rescheduled to Saturday Amid Severe Weather Warning
item.description: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, celebrating its 100th anniversary, has been postponed to Saturday due to severe weather conditions forecasted for Thanksgiving Day. Officials cited safety concerns as the primary reason for the delay, with the National Weather Service predicting heavy rain, strong winds, and coastal flooding along the East Coast. The parade, which typically takes place on Thanksgiving morning, will now begin at 8:30 a.m. ET on Saturday. Macy's stated that the decision was made after consultation with city and agency partners, emphasizing that the safety of participants and spectators remains their top priority. Mayor Zohran Mamdani warned New Yorkers about the impending storm, with sustained winds of 30-40 mph and potential gusts up to 65 mph, prompting high-wind and coastal flood warnings. item.title: Hera mission discovers stadium-sized crater on asteroid Dimorphos from DART impact
item.description: The European Space Agency's Hera mission has discovered a stadium-sized crater on the asteroid Dimorphos, which was created by the impact of NASA's DART spacecraft in September 2022. Dimorphos, a 151-meter diameter asteroid orbiting the larger Didymos asteroid, has undergone significant changes following the DART impact. The crater spans the entire width of Dimorphos, flattening the impact side of the asteroid. While the crater is the most visible change, the asteroid also shows chaotic rotation and is surrounded by hundreds of previously unknown rocks. The DART mission, which impacted Dimorphos on September 26, 2022, successfully shortened the asteroid's orbital period by 33 minutes, exceeding expectations. However, the physical changes to Dimorphos remained unknown until Hera's observations. item.title: Historic Brooklyn Townhouse Next to Norman Mailer's Former Residence Lists for $13.5 Million
item.description: A historic 19th-century townhouse in Brooklyn, New York, which was once next door to the former residence of Pulitzer Prize-winning author Norman Mailer, is now on the market for $13.5 million. The property, built in 1856 and measuring 8,249 square feet, has been owned by the same family for nearly 70 years. The family is selling after the death of their 101-year-old matriarch earlier this year. The townhouse features nine bedrooms, six bathrooms, and a variety of architectural elements including original fireplaces, 10-foot-high windows with wooden shutters, and a New Orleans-style terrace with wrought-iron railings. The listing agent, Linda VanderWoude of Brown Harris Stevens, highlighted that the property is one of only four contiguous townhouses with the same wrought-iron railing on the parlor floor. item.title: Octopuses Employ Multi-Step Squeezing Technique for Confined Spaces
item.description: Octopuses, known for their remarkable flexibility, have been found to use a sophisticated multi-step process to navigate through tight spaces, according to a recent study published in the Journal of Experimental Biology. Researchers observed that common octopuses and Maya octopuses employ different strategies depending on the size of the opening. For larger gaps, the octopuses typically use a three-step process: exploring the hole with their arms, inserting two arms through first, and then threading the remaining limbs and mantle through the opening. For smaller gaps, they switch to a four-step method involving body rotation, widening the passage by pushing arm bases deeper into the hole, twisting and stretching arms to feed them through, and finally sliding the head through with tentacle leverage. item.title: Yayoi Kusama's Phallic Artwork Challenged Male Dominance in the Art World
item.description: Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama, who died on August 14, 2026, at age 97, spent her career challenging the Western, male-dominated art world through her innovative and controversial installations. Her work, particularly the Accumulation series, featured sewn phallic protrusions that subverted traditional gender symbolism. Kusama's approach was a deliberate artistic choice rather than a manifestation of obsessive-compulsive disorder, as critics often assumed. She used traditionally feminine crafts like sewing to create phallic forms, upholstering furniture with these elements to transform domestic spaces into sites of gender critique. Her 1962 work Accumulation No. 1, which featured sewn phallic shapes on an armchair, marked a pivotal moment in her career and the art world. While male artists like Claes Oldenburg received immediate acclaim for similar works, Kusama's contributions were initially overlooked. item.title: Sarcopenia: Preventing Muscle Loss and Functional Decline in Aging
item.description: Sarcopenia, the progressive loss of muscle mass, strength, and function associated with aging, is a growing health concern among older adults. This condition significantly increases the risk of frailty, falls, disability, and loss of independence. Recent research emphasizes the importance of early detection and a multifaceted approach to prevention and management. The most effective strategies include resistance exercise, proper nutrition, and functional recovery programs. Resistance training has been shown to increase muscle mass and improve strength and physical function in older adults with sarcopenia. It promotes muscle protein synthesis, enhances neuromuscular coordination, and improves the muscle's response to maintenance stimuli. Programs like Vivifrail, developed at the Public University of Navarra, combine strength, endurance, balance, and walking exercises tailored to individual capabilities. item.title: Belgian Artist Henri Joseph Thomas Captures Belle Époque Elegance in Timeless Portraits
item.description: Henri Joseph Thomas (1878–1972), a Belgian painter, sculptor, and etcher, is celebrated for his refined and alluring depictions of women during the Belle Époque and interwar periods. Born in Molenbeek-Saint-Jean, Thomas trained at the Académie Royale des Beaux-Arts in Brussels, initially working as an illustrator before transitioning to painting. His artistic repertoire includes elegant portrayals of ladies, cabaret dancers, and intimate café scenes, blending sophistication with subtle temptation and decadence. Thomas also created delicate floral still lifes and portraits characterized by graceful composition and atmospheric charm. These works capture the elegance and quiet allure of the Belle Époque era, reflecting Thomas's unique ability to chronicle the period's essence. His notable pieces include 'Reclining Woman with a Veil,' 'Reverie,' 'The Green Shoes,' 'Daydreaming,' 'Adornment,' 'At the Theatre,' 'Before the Ball,' 'Courtesans at the Bar,' 'Dancer in a Black Dress,' 'Dressed f

item.title: Thanksgiving Art: Dinner Plated Like 10 Famous Artists
item.description: Hannah Rothstein, an artist known for her viral and humorous work, created a series called 'Thanksgiving Special' in 2014 where she reimagined a traditional Thanksgiving dinner through the lens of ten famous artists. Each plate featured the same core ingredients—turkey, stuffing, mashed potatoes, gravy, green beans, corn, and cranberry sauce—but presented in the distinctive styles of artists such as René Magritte, Piet Mondrian, Mark Rothko, Georges Seurat, Vincent van Gogh, Andy Warhol, Jackson Pollock, Pablo Picasso, Julian Schnabel, and Cindy Sherman. For instance, Magritte's influence was seen in a plate where gravy formed a pipe-like shape with the caption 'Ceci n'est pas un repas' (This is not a meal), while Mondrian's geometric grids were recreated using cranberry red, corn yellow, and potato white. item.title: Deep-Sea Brine Pools Discovered in Red Sea Gulf of Aqaba
item.description: Researchers from the University of Miami's Rosenstiel School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Earth Science have discovered rare deep-sea brine pools more than a mile beneath the surface of the Red Sea in the Gulf of Aqaba. These extremely salty, oxygen-free environments, known as brine pools, are teeming with microbial life despite their harsh conditions. The discovery was made using a remotely operated underwater vehicle (ROV) during a four-week expedition aboard the OceanXplorer research vessel. The pools, located at a depth of 1,770 meters, represent the first documented discovery of such formations in the Gulf of Aqaba. The research team, led by Professor Sam Purkis, noted that these environments could provide insights into Earth's ancient oceans and aid in the search for extraterrestrial life. item.description: JemRec is a free, open-source call recording application designed for unrooted Android devices, offering a solution for users who need to record phone and messenger calls without requiring root access. The app addresses common challenges with call recording on Android, such as compatibility with different network types (2G, VoLTE, Wi-Fi Calling), handling of locked screens, and the need for specific developer settings. JemRec requires certain configurations, including enabling Wireless Debugging and adjusting USB settings to prevent interruptions during calls. The app is not available on Google Play due to policy changes that prohibit the use of the Accessibility API for call recording, but it can be downloaded from F-Droid or GitHub. JemRec emphasizes user privacy and control, with recordings stored in standard folders and no data collection. item.title: Rare Color Photographs Reveal Daily Life Under Jim Crow in 1950s South
item.description: The American South during the 1950s was defined by a rigid system of racial segregation enforced through Jim Crow laws, which affected nearly every aspect of daily life for Black Americans. Two LIFE magazine photo essays from 1956, captured by photographers Gordon Parks in Alabama and Margaret Bourke-White in South Carolina, provide a rare color documentation of this era. Parks focused on Black families in Alabama, photographing their homes, work, and daily routines to reveal how segregation permeated ordinary life rather than focusing on protests or violence. His 26-image series, 'The Restraints: Open and Hidden,' published in September 1956, offered an intimate look at the personal impacts of discrimination. Most of Parks' original work was believed lost until 2011, when over 70 color transparencies were discovered, leading to the publication of 'The Segregation Story.' item.title: Cahokia's Climate-Driven Shifts Mirror Modern Community Challenges in Illinois
item.description: More than 800 years ago, the Mississippian people of Cahokia, a massive archaeological site near modern-day St. Louis, faced environmental and societal challenges that led to gradual depopulation. Recent research by anthropologists Sissel Schroeder and the author reveals parallels between Cahokia's decline and the current situation in Centreville, Illinois, where residents are abandoning their homes due to climate-driven flooding and outdated infrastructure. Cahokia, at its peak around 1100 CE, housed up to 20,000 people and featured Monks Mound, the largest prehistoric earthwork in the Americas. Archaeological evidence shows that during the Medieval Climatic Anomaly, Cahokia experienced severe droughts and floods, leading to a slow population decline over two centuries. Similarly, Centreville has seen increased rainfall (10 inches more annually since the 1960s) causing frequent flooding, backed-up sewage, and deteriorating infrastructure. item.title: Marilyn Monroe's Ankle Injury and Support from Allan 'Whitey' Snyder During 1953 Film Production
item.description: During the summer of 1953, while filming Otto Preminger's Western 'River of No Return' in the Canadian Rockies, Marilyn Monroe suffered a severe ankle injury that required a cast and crutches. Behind-the-scenes photographs from the production frequently depict her being assisted across rugged terrain by her personal makeup artist and close confidant, Allan 'Whitey' Snyder, as well as co-star Robert Mitchum and crew members. The injury occurred when Monroe slipped on a submerged rock while wearing chest-high rubber hip waders during a Bow River scene rehearsal. The heavy waders filled with water, pinning her down, and she severely sprained her ankle and tore ligaments. Despite the injury, filming continued due to a tight schedule, with Monroe's leg in a plaster cast and using wooden crutches between takes. item.title: Historical Zoo Practice: Oil Polishing of Tortoise Shells at London Zoo in the 1920s
item.description: During the early-to-mid 20th century, the London Zoo implemented a routine grooming practice known as 'lustering' or polishing tortoise shells, which was performed regularly during spring and summer months. Keepers applied oil to the shells of giant tortoises, believing it would condition the shells, prevent dryness or cracking, and provide a clean, glossy appearance for visitors. The specific oil used was Duckham's Adcol / Arkoil (labeled Parkoil in this batch), a highly refined mineral oil produced by British lubricant company Alexander Duckham & Co. This oil was famously marketed as being so pure and harmless that it could be used to lubricate 'a baby, a watch, or an elephant.' The grooming sessions were not only part of the zoo's care routine but also became popular public demonstrations, drawing crowds of curious onlookers to watch the massive Galápagos and Aldabra tortoises receive their seasonal shine. The findings revealed only five brooches matched the mold fragments, suggesting brooch production was widespread beyond major settlements. Instead of standardized 'fast-fashion' items, Viking artisans created unique pieces with differentiated motifs, such as the 'gripping beasts' design featuring intertwined animals. item.description: Fern Andra, born Vernal Edna Andrews on November 24, 1893, was an American actress, film director, scriptwriter, and producer who became one of the most prominent figures in German silent cinema during the 1910s and 1920s. Starting as a child tightrope walker in American circuses and vaudeville, she traveled to Europe around 1912–1913 and caught the attention of theater director Max Reinhardt in Berlin. Her film debut came in 1913 with 'Das Ave Maria,' directed by and co-starring German pioneer Zelnik. During World War I, when foreign films were banned in Germany, Andra remained in the country and rose to prominence, rivaling popular actresses like Asta Nielsen and Henny Porten. By 1915–1916, she established her own production company, Fern Andra-Film, often writing, co-directing, and producing her own films, such as 'Ernst ist das Leben' (1916) and 'Es fiel ein Reif in der Frühlingsnacht' (1915), where she performed her own high-wire stunts. item.title: Traditional Naxi River Transport Using Goat-Skin Rafts Documented by Joseph Rock in 1928
item.description: Austrian-American explorer and botanist Joseph Rock, who spent decades documenting indigenous cultures, flora, and landscapes of southwestern China for the National Geographic Society and Harvard University, captured a unique river transport method during his 1928 expedition in Yunnan. The photograph depicts Naxi ferrymen using traditional skin rafts to transport heavy expedition supplies across treacherous river gorges where bridges were nonexistent. Known historically in China as huntuo, these skin rafts have been used on turbulent rivers like the Yellow and upper Yangtze for over 2,000 years. The construction process involved carefully removing goat or sheep skin in one piece, sealing all openings except one leg, treating it with oil and salt for waterproofing and flexibility, and inflating it by mouth. item.title: Archaeologists Uncover Gallic Coin Hoard and Ritual Artifacts at Iron Age Sanctuary Site
item.description: Archaeologists from France's National Institute for Preventive Archaeological Research (Inrap) have uncovered a significant Iron Age discovery near Bure in the Meuse department, northeastern France. The excavation, conducted during preventive work for the Cigéo deep geological storage project, revealed a timber building from the Late La Tène period, approximately 2,000 years old, which may have functioned as a sanctuary. Within the structure, researchers found 28 Gallic potins—cast coins widely used in north-eastern Gaul during the Late Iron Age—along with a miniature metal wheel and fragments of a human skull. The coins, featuring stylized human heads derived from Philip II of Macedon's portraits and boar-shaped military standards, provide insight into Gallic artistic and cultural practices. item.description:
Astronomers from Chalmers University of Technology have made groundbreaking discoveries about how red giant stars like Mira spread key elements such as carbon, oxygen, and nitrogen through the Milky Way. Using the ALMA telescope in Chile, the international research team captured unprecedented detail of Mira, a red giant star located 330 light years from Earth in the constellation Cetus. The study, published in Astronomy & Astrophysics, reveals that magnetic fields, not starlight as previously believed, power the stellar winds that disperse these essential elements.
The research team observed a record-breaking stellar eruption in 2023 that created a massive gas loop extending 10 astronomical units from Mira—equivalent to the distance from the Sun to Saturn. This loop, imaged in 2025, provided critical evidence that magnetic fields shape and propel stellar winds. item.title: Hair Ice: A Rare Natural Phenomenon Created by Fungi and Frost
item.description: Hair ice, a rare natural phenomenon that resembles silky white hair growing from logs, has been studied for over a century. First observed by Alfred Wegener in 1916, the phenomenon was initially attributed to a fungus, but it wasn't until 2015 that researchers confirmed the role of the fungus Exidiopsis effusa. This fungus, found on rotting hardwood, enables the formation of delicate ice strands that can reach up to eight inches in length. The ice forms when water inside decaying wood is pulled to the surface on cold, still nights just below freezing. The fungus appears to prevent the ice strands from fusing together, resulting in thousands of separate, hair-like filaments. Hair ice has been reported in various locations across the Northern Hemisphere, including Scotland, Ireland, Germany, Switzerland, Canada, and the United States, particularly in regions between 45 and 55 degrees north latitude. This 'gap' in the mass distribution aligns with theoretical predictions about black holes formed from stars that never exploded. The study, published in Physical Review D, indicates that these black holes may represent a distinct population formed through 'failed supernovae'—a process where stars collapse silently without the explosive death typically associated with massive stars. item.description: Scientists from Texas A&M University have discovered that a key component of DNA, thymine, may have played a crucial role in helping early life survive Earth's intense ultraviolet radiation. This finding resolves a long-standing evolutionary mystery about why DNA evolved to use thymine despite its increased susceptibility to UV damage compared to uracil. item.title: Habitat 67: A Half-Century-Old Architectural Experiment in Montreal
item.description: Habitat 67, a residential complex designed by Israeli-Canadian architect Moshe Safdie, stands as one of the most distinctive architectural landmarks in Montreal, Quebec. Originally conceived as Safdie's master's thesis at McGill University in 1961, the project evolved into a centerpiece of Expo 67, the 1967 World's Fair held in Montreal. The complex, composed of 354 prefabricated concrete modules arranged in a staggered, puzzle-like formation, was intended to merge suburban living qualities with urban density. Each of the 158 apartments, ranging from one to eight connected modules, featured private outdoor terraces of varying sizes, offering residents a sense of space and privacy often missing in high-rise developments. Construction began in 1964, and the structure opened to the public in April 1967, becoming one of the fair's most popular attractions. item.title: Current Smoking Linked to Higher Dementia Risk, Study Finds
item.description: A comprehensive review and meta-analysis of 61 prospective cohort studies involving approximately 2.8 million participants has found that current smoking is associated with a significantly increased risk of all-cause dementia, Alzheimer's disease, and vascular dementia. The study, published in eClinicalMedicine, updates previous research by incorporating data from studies conducted between 2013 and 2026, expanding on the 2015 review that included 34 studies. Current smokers showed a 31% higher risk of all-cause dementia (RR 1.31 [95% CI 1.23–1.39]), a 40% higher risk of Alzheimer's disease (RR 1.40 [1.08–1.80]), and a 52% higher risk of vascular dementia (RR 1.52 [1.20–1.93]) compared to non-smokers. Former smokers, however, did not show an increased risk for any dementia outcome and had a lower risk of all-cause dementia than current smokers (RR 0.81 [0.75–0.88]). item.description: The European Space Agency (ESA) and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) have become the second and third space agencies, respectively, to successfully place a spacecraft into orbit around Mercury, following NASA's MESSENGER mission in March 2011. Harden, who made all 14 of his free throws, also recorded six rebounds and six assists in the game at Rocket Arena. This performance marks his first 50-point game since scoring 55 points for the Los Angeles Clippers in November 2025. Wilt Chamberlain holds the record with 118 such games, while Michael Jordan is second with 31. Harden, the ninth highest scorer in NBA history with 29,633 points, reflected on his evolution as a player, noting that at 37, he has adapted his game to remain impactful despite reduced speed and agility. item.title: Hayabusa 2 Adjusts Mission to Target 2015 BM510 After Ion Engine Issues
item.description: The Hayabusa 2 spacecraft has changed its target asteroid from 1998 KY26 to 2015 BM510 due to issues with its ion engines. Originally planned to reach 1998 KY26 in 2031 for detailed exploration, the mission now will conduct a high-speed flyby of 2015 BM510 in April 2028. The change was necessitated by a problem with the ion engines, which forced cancellation of the encounter with 1998 KY26. Hayabusa 2, launched on December 3, 2014, successfully returned samples from asteroid Ryugu in December 2020, beginning its extended mission. Recently, on July 5, 2026, it performed a close flyby of asteroid (98943) Torifune at 400 meters, the closest high-speed flyby of a Solar System body to date. The spacecraft carries four ion engines (A, B, C, D) with a combined Delta-V of 2 km/s. However, three of the neutralizers failed after 7,000-10,000 hours of operation due to unexpected degradation. item.title: Signal Limits Mobile Screenshot Functionality Amid AI Surveillance Concerns
item.description: Signal, the secure messaging app, has announced new restrictions on mobile screenshot functionality as part of its response to what it describes as an 'existential threat' posed by operating systems integrating agentic AI. President Meredith Whittaker explained that platforms like Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS are now enabling AI agents to scan users' screens, capturing sensitive data without Signal's control. This data is stored locally or sent to remote servers, potentially compromising the privacy of all conversation participants. Signal had previously blocked screenshots in its Windows app by default, but now extends this restriction to Android and iOS. Users can disable this setting, though Whittaker warned it would 'break our privacy guarantees.' She also acknowledged the solution is 'incomplete,' as it doesn't address other potential ways AI agents might access application data. item.title: AI Debt Collection Platform Reveals Data Vulnerability Affecting Millions
item.description: A security researcher discovered two critical vulnerabilities in CreditNirvana, an AI-driven debt collection platform used by major Indian financial services firms. The flaws, which were patched in June but publicly disclosed in October, exposed 6.6 million borrower accounts and 315,000 call recordings containing sensitive personal and financial information. The high-severity vulnerability compromised call center data, including recommendations generated after calls, while the critical vulnerability exposed corporate customer data, credit reports, ID documents, legal records, and communications such as emails and texts. CERT-In, India's cybersecurity agency, classified one as 'high' and the other as 'critical' severity. The researcher, Eaton Zveare, collaborated with CERT-In to resolve the issues, noting that the platform's AI-driven automation for debt collection—designed to 'read a borrower's full context, decide the next best action, and execute it autonomously'—created significant

item.title: Hollywood Actresses Amy Irving, Carrie Fisher, and Teri Garr Celebrate Friendship at 1977 New York City Gathering
item.description: In 1977, New York City's social scene hosted a notable gathering featuring three prominent Hollywood actresses: Amy Irving, Carrie Fisher, and Teri Garr. item.description: Google has created a controlled, alternate-universe internet environment called the 'Mirror Dimension' to safely train AI browsing agents for Chrome. This isolated web ecosystem, detailed in a recent blog post, includes realistic websites and platforms such as social media, shopping sites, and bank dashboards, all designed to mimic the real internet's complexity. The Chrome team built this environment to address challenges in training AI agents, as traditional testing in limited environments is ineffective due to 'eval awareness'—where agents behave differently knowing they're in a test—and risking uncontrolled deployment on the open web. The Mirror Dimension allows agents to navigate and interact with simulated sites while facing resilience tests, including hidden prompt-injection attacks, to strengthen their defenses. item.description: A recent leak suggests that Samsung is developing its own version of the iPhone's Dynamic Island feature, which has been a distinctive element of Apple's user interface. item.title: Etna Volcano Summit Hosts Unique Convergence of Ten Municipal Boundaries
item.description: The summit of Mount Etna in Sicily, Italy, is the only place on Earth where ten different municipal boundaries converge. This unique geographical feature, known as a 'decipoint,' is a result of historical land division practices. The article explains that the Etna volcano, Europe's most active volcano, has been a source of wealth for surrounding communities for centuries, particularly through agriculture and the harvesting of snow for refrigeration. The ten municipalities sharing the summit—Adrano, Biancavilla, Belpasso, Bronte (counted twice due to two different angles), Castiglione di Sicilia, Maletto, Nicolosi, Randazzo, Sant'Alfio, and Zafferana Etnea—divided the mountain's slopes to avoid conflicts over resources. The article notes that while twelve localities are in the shadow of Etna, only ten have boundaries extending to the summit. item.description: Entain, the London-listed owner of Ladbrokes and Coral, is in advanced negotiations to sell its 47.5% stake in its central and eastern European operations to CVC Capital Partners. The deal, which could value the entire division between £1.5 billion and £1.75 billion, aims to mitigate the financial impact of recent UK government tax increases on the gambling industry. The company's central and eastern European business, primarily comprising sports betting operations in Croatia and Poland, was formed through a joint venture with EMMA Capital, initially established in 2022 after acquiring Croatia's SuperSport and expanding in 2023 with the £750 million purchase of STS in Poland. Entain had previously sold a 20% stake to EMMA Capital for £366 million in June, retaining a 47.5% interest. item.description: The stock market experienced a significant downturn on November 20, 2026, with technology stocks leading the decline. Nvidia and Anthropic, two prominent companies in the artificial intelligence sector, saw their stock prices drop sharply. This market movement follows a period of strong performance in the AI industry, particularly after Anthropic's recent successful market debut. Despite the current slump, analysts note that the broader U.S. economy remains robust, with few anticipating a recession in the near term. Inflation continues to be viewed as a short-term concern rather than a long-term threat, allowing investors to seek out attractive real yields. item.title: ESA's Hera Probe Begins Detailed Study of Asteroid System After NASA's DART Impact Test
item.description: The European Space Agency's Hera probe has reached the Didymos binary asteroid system, where NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission impacted Dimorphos in 2022. This marks the first time a spacecraft has returned to study the aftermath of a planetary defense test. The DART mission, launched in 2021, successfully altered Dimorphos' orbit by 33 minutes through a high-speed collision, demonstrating the feasibility of deflecting potentially hazardous asteroids. Hera's mission includes detailed examination of the impact site, measurement of Dimorphos' mass, and analysis of the binary system's formation. The probe carries two CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, designed to land on Dimorphos and conduct geophysical and compositional studies. Hera's instruments will map the asteroids' topography with 1-meter resolution and investigate surface chemistry. item.title: Ancient Greek Colony in Sicily Revealed Early Weaning and Extended Breastfeeding Practices
item.description: A groundbreaking study published in the European Journal of Archaeology has uncovered evidence that infants in the ancient Greek colony of Himera, located in Sicily, began consuming solid foods as early as three months but continued breastfeeding for nearly four years. The research, led by biological anthropologist Laurie Reitsema from the University of Georgia, analyzed chemical signatures in the bones of 58 children and 27 adult women from the site. Carbon and nitrogen isotopes revealed that babies started solid foods around three months, significantly earlier than the recommendations of ancient physicians like Galen and Soranus, who suggested weaning at 1.5 to 3 years. However, breastfeeding persisted for approximately 3.8 years, much longer than in most preindustrial societies. While some leaders express frustration with Trump's continued influence, others acknowledge his undeniable sway over the party base. item.description: Jason Fulford's latest book, 'Frozen Features,' delves into the artist's unique approach to photomontage, where he combines random photographs from his personal archive to create unexpected visual narratives. The book, published by Loose Joints, emerged from Fulford's spontaneous process of selecting images from a folder of approximately 10,000 scanned negatives without viewing thumbnails, allowing chance to guide his creative decisions. This method, which Fulford describes as 'gambling' with images, led him to discover surprising connections between seemingly unrelated photographs, creating what he calls 'enigmas' that resist simple interpretation. item.description: The first meeting of a powerful health advisory panel with appointees of Robert F. Kennedy Jr. (RFK Jr.) was marked by significant tension and disagreement. item.title: Eleanor Powell: The Queen of Tap in 1930s Hollywood
item.description: Eleanor Torrey Powell (November 21, 1912 – February 11, 1982) was an American dancer and actress who rose to prominence in the 1930s as MGM's top female dancing star, earning the title 'Queen of Tap.' Unlike many female dancers of her era who were primarily cast as romantic partners, Powell was billed as a solo performer whose athletic, machine-gun footwork became a hallmark of major studio musicals. Starting her career in Broadway revues in 1929, Powell quickly gained recognition for her rapid, precise rhythm, earning the title 'the world's greatest tap dancer' during her early 1930s stage work. Her film debut came in Fox's George White's 1935 Scandals, though she initially considered the experience a disaster due to a makeup mix-up that left her styled to look Egyptian. item.title: Democrats Make Inroads in Republican Strongholds of the Deep South Despite Redistricting Efforts
item.description:
The 2022 midterm elections revealed significant shifts in the political landscape of the Deep South, where Democrats made unexpected gains in traditionally Republican areas. Tennessee state Rep. Justin Pearson narrowly lost his congressional race to Republican Brent Taylor by about one percentage point in a newly redrawn district that was expected to be a Republican stronghold. item.title: Understanding the Distinction Between Disc and Disk in Technology
item.description: The article explores the subtle yet significant difference between the spelling of 'disc' and 'disk' in technology terminology. While both terms refer to storage media, they represent fundamentally different technologies. The term 'disk' with a 'k' typically refers to magnetic storage devices such as traditional hard drives and floppy disks, which use mechanical parts to read and write data. In contrast, 'disc' with a 'c' is used for optical storage media like DVDs, Blu-ray discs, and CDs, which rely on laser technology to access data. The article clarifies that while SSDs (solid-state drives) are often referred to as 'disks,' they technically differ from traditional magnetic disks due to their use of NAND flash memory without moving parts. item.title: Grandmother's Persistent Cough Led to Early Lung Cancer Diagnosis
item.description: Wendy Robinson, a 54-year-old grandmother from Cleethorpes, recently shared her experience of how she initially dismissed a persistent dry cough as a normal symptom of being an ex-smoker, only to discover it was an early sign of lung cancer. After being diagnosed with stage 2 lung cancer during a routine follow-up for previous kidney cancer, Robinson emphasized the importance of not ignoring persistent symptoms. She stated, 'I had a constant cough, nothing too harsh, just one dry little cough. I thought it was because I was an ex-smoker, so I didn’t go to the GP as I assumed it was just a smoker’s cough.' Robinson, who is now a grandmother, expressed gratitude for being able to meet her first grandchild after successful treatment. The Humber and North Yorkshire Cancer Alliance is using her story as part of its 'Get Ahead of Cancer' campaign, which aims to challenge the common tendency to dismiss potential cancer symptoms. item.title: Dentist Identifies Smooth Tongue as Potential Indicator of Anemia
item.description: Anemia is a common blood disorder affecting approximately six percent of people in the UK, characterized by insufficient healthy red blood cells to transport oxygen throughout the body. While symptoms such as fatigue, shortness of breath, and pale skin are well-known, dental professionals have identified additional oral indicators that may signal anemia. Dr. Jas Sagoo, a dentist from Perfect Smile Spa, emphasizes that during routine dental check-ups, dentists often notice warning signs in the mouth, including pale gums and smooth or glossy patches on the tongue. These changes, along with mouth sores and cracked corners of the lips, can serve as early indicators of anemia, a condition that, if left untreated, can strain vital organs due to reduced oxygen supply. Anemia can range from mild to severe, with various types stemming from different underlying causes. item.title: Geological Record Reveals 405,000-Year Cycle in Ancient Storm Activity Linked to Orbital Patterns
item.description: Scientists have identified a 405,000-year cycle in ancient storm activity preserved in geological records, suggesting a connection to Earth's orbital patterns. The research, led by geologist Shuyuan Shi from China's Research Institute of Petroleum Exploration and Development, analyzed sedimentary rocks from China's Sichuan Basin, which date back approximately 500 million years. Using cyclostratigraphy—a technique that identifies repeating patterns in sedimentary layers—the team reconstructed about 24 million years of geological history. They found 59 cycles of roughly 405,000 years each, with tempestites (storm deposits) clustering during the rising and peak phases of these cycles. These periods featured thicker, coarser deposits, indicating more intense storm activity, while thinner, finer deposits appeared during the opposite phases. item.title: Texas execution of Reinaldo Dennes takes over an hour amid vein-finding difficulties
item.description: Reinaldo Dennes, a 70-year-old death row inmate convicted of murder in a 1996 diamond robbery in Houston, experienced a prolonged and painful execution process in Texas that lasted over an hour. During the lethal injection at Huntsville Unit state prison on Thursday, Dennes reportedly screamed in pain, described 'the pain,' and repeatedly asked for mercy, saying 'let me go, father.' Witnesses noted he complained about severe pain in his right leg, cramps, and made loud groans. Prison spokesperson Amanda Hernandez acknowledged multiple unsuccessful attempts to locate a suitable vein for the sedative pentobarbital, eventually inserting needles into his left foot and neck. Hernandez suggested Dennes may have exaggerated the pain, noting it was not the first time inmates made such claims before drugs were properly administered. The execution began at 5:44 p.m. and concluded at 7:07 p.m., 63 minutes after Dennes was strapped to the hospital trolley. He was pronounced dead one minute later.

item.title: Fifth Circuit Rules Congress Violated Quorum Clause in Passing Pregnant Workers' Law
item.description: The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals has ruled that Congress violated the Constitution's quorum clause when passing the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act, effectively halting its enforcement in Texas, Louisiana, and Mississippi. The court determined that the law, which was included in a $1.7 trillion spending bill during the pandemic, was passed using proxy and remote voting, which the judges deemed unconstitutional. The ruling, issued 9-8, states that the quorum clause requires a majority of members to be physically present, and proxy votes do not count toward quorum. Legal experts warn this decision could invalidate the entire spending bill, including $858 billion in defense spending, and may lead to nationwide challenges against other legislation passed under similar pandemic-era voting procedures. item.title: WordPress Plugin Vulnerability Allows Stored XSS for Subscribers
item.description: A critical security vulnerability has been identified in the CodePeople Post Map for Google Maps plugin for WordPress, affecting versions up to 1.3.0. The flaw, designated as CVE-2026-133369, allows authenticated subscribers to inject malicious scripts through the 'api_key' setting, resulting in a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) attack. This vulnerability impacts users who have the plugin installed and configured with the affected version, potentially compromising user data and website integrity. The issue was reported by security@wordfence.com and documented in the National Vulnerability Database (NVD). The vulnerability is classified under CWE-79, which refers to improper neutralization of user input. The plugin's code, specifically in the functions.php file and cpm.admin.js, fails to sanitize user input for the 'api_key' parameter, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript code within the context of the website. item.title: Dose-Dependent Effects of Nickel Oxide Nanoparticles on Atrazine Uptake and Oxidative Stress in Soybean Plants
item.description: A recent study published in the journal Emerging Contaminants has revealed that nickel oxide nanoparticles (NiO-NPs) have a dose-dependent effect on the accumulation and toxicity of atrazine in soybean plants. Researchers from the Northeast Institute of Geography and Agroecology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and Jilin Normal University conducted experiments exposing soybean plants to atrazine in soil amended with NiO-NPs at concentrations of 5, 50, and 100 mg per kilogram. The findings showed that at lower concentrations (5 and 50 mg/kg), NiO-NPs reduced atrazine accumulation and alleviated oxidative stress caused by the herbicide. However, at the higher concentration of 100 mg/kg, the opposite effect was observed: plants accumulated more atrazine and exhibited increased oxidative stress compared to exposure to atrazine alone. item.title: Potatoes Grown in Simulated Lunar Soil Yield Comparable Nutrition to Earth-Grown Varieties
item.description: A groundbreaking study conducted by botanists at Oregon State University (OSU) has demonstrated that potatoes can be successfully cultivated in simulated lunar regolith, with results showing comparable nutritional value to potatoes grown on Earth. The research, published in the journal npj Microgravity, involved mixing simulated moon soil with vermicompost—a nutrient-rich soil produced by worms—to create a viable growing medium. The team discovered that a mixture containing just 30% vermicompost was sufficient to produce potato crops with yields similar to those achieved in Earth-based agriculture. This finding is significant for future lunar missions, as it addresses a critical challenge in sustaining human life on the Moon: the need for reliable, nutritious food sources. The study also confirmed that potatoes grown in this simulated lunar environment did not exhibit elevated levels of glycoalkaloids, natural toxins that can cause discoloration and potential health issues. item.description: The German engineering company ZF has unveiled a new electric motor technology called the High Revolution Drive, capable of spinning at 30,000 rpm. Conventional EV motors typically operate at around 18,000 rpm, requiring large, heavy rotors with expensive rare-earth magnets to generate sufficient torque. item.description: Researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign recently conducted a digital imaging workshop at the Rare Book and Manuscript Library (RBML) to uncover hidden information in medieval manuscripts using multispectral imaging technology. The workshop, organized by Illinois history professor Kalani Craig and RBML curator Cait Coker, served as a pilot study for analyzing fragile, centuries-old documents. The technology employs multiple wavelengths of light to recover faint ink traces that are otherwise illegible. One notable manuscript examined was a parchment leaf from an eighth-century French abbey tax record, which had a sixth- or seventh-century Greek papyrus glued to its back. The deteriorated papyrus, the oldest surviving papyrus north of the Alps, contained a poem with faint ink that the imaging process aimed to clarify. The workshop also imaged a 1530-1566 Italian portolan chart mapping the Mediterranean, seeking evidence of salt residue that might indicate maritime use.

item.title: Scientists Develop Method to Detect Mirror Life Threat Using Polarized Light
item.description: Scientists are concerned about the potential threat of 'mirror life'—hypothetical organisms built from mirror-image molecules that could evade immune systems and pose a biosecurity risk. A research team from the University of Strathclyde and Durham University has proposed a detection method using circularly polarized luminescence (CPL), which analyzes the chirality of molecules. Living organisms typically use only one enantiomer (mirror-image form) of key molecules, but mirror life could bypass biological defenses. The method involves fluorescent probes that bind to cellular structures and emit light with a specific rotational direction based on the molecule's handedness. Ordinary biological molecules would produce a different light signature than mirror-image counterparts, allowing detection. La sonda, lanzada en 1977, ha explorado el sistema solar exterior, realizando observaciones cercanas de Júpiter y Saturno, y luego de la luna Titan y los anillos de Saturno. Voyager 1 cruzó el espacio interestelar en agosto de 2012 y continúa recopilando datos sobre el campo magnético, densidad de plasma y partículas energéticas. Los científicos están particularmente interesados en cómo la influencia del Sol cambia a medida que la sonda se aleja, y si podrá determinar dónde termina la influencia solar y comienza el espacio interestelar prístino. A pesar de que cada Voyager pierde 4 vatios de potencia anualmente, la misión ha implementado estrategias de gestión de energía, incluyendo una redistribución de potencia 'Big Bang' realizada este año para preservar la ciencia. item.description: The article discusses the ongoing legal battle between major news organizations, including The New York Times, and AI companies like OpenAI and Microsoft over the use of copyrighted materials in training AI systems. The Department of Justice (DOJ) has sided with OpenAI, arguing that requiring copyright licenses for AI training would impose high costs and hinder innovation, particularly for small companies. However, the author argues that this position contradicts the White House's AI framework and G20 principles, which recognize the importance of copyright protections for creators. The article highlights the bipartisan CLEAR Act, introduced by Senators Adam Schiff and John Curtis, which would require AI developers to publicly disclose the copyrighted works used in their training datasets. This transparency would allow creators to seek compensation when their works are used without permission. item.description: The article discusses a collection of 36 Polaroid photographs taken by Sean Young during the filming of Blade Runner in 1981, which was released in 1982. Young recalled being overwhelmed by the scale of the sets while navigating the stressful atmosphere. item.title: International Court Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya, Setting Precedent for Global Accountability
item.description: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) delivered a landmark ruling on November 19, 2026, determining that Myanmar's military, the Tatmadaw, committed genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority. This historic judgment, stemming from a case filed by Gambia in 2019, marks the first time the ICJ has ruled that a state is legally responsible for committing genocide rather than merely failing to prevent it. The court found that Myanmar's 'clearance operations' in 2017, which involved the destruction of Rohingya villages, mass killings, sexual violence, and forced displacement, met the legal definition of genocide under the 1948 UN Genocide Convention. The ruling established that the military's actions demonstrated specific intent to destroy the Rohingya ethnic group, not just counterinsurgency efforts. item.title: La AUGC denuncia amenazas de muerte contra los guardias civiles heridos en el choque con una narcolancha en el Guadalquivir
item.description:

Entre los mensajes compartidos aparecen expresiones como «a ver si con suerte le traspasa el palo del radar por el pecho» y comentarios que celebran que la patrullera Río Corneja haya quedado fuera de servicio. La AUGC ha condenado estas manifestaciones y ha reclamado más medios materiales, protección y respaldo institucional para los agentes que combaten el narcotráfico.

item.title: Los factores políticos que explican la pérdida de apoyos de Irene Montero dentro de la izquierda
item.description:
Irene Montero atraviesa una etapa de pérdida de apoyos dentro del espacio político situado a la izquierda del PSOE. Un artículo de opinión firmado por Iñaki Errazkin analiza los principales motivos de este desgaste y sostiene que las críticas a la dirigente de Podemos ya no proceden únicamente de la derecha, sino también de antiguos simpatizantes, sectores feministas y otras organizaciones progresistas.
Uno de los principales factores señalados es la gestión de la Ley Orgánica de Garantía Integral de la Libertad Sexual, conocida como ley del solo sí es sí. Su aplicación provocó revisiones a la baja de numerosas condenas a agresores sexuales, lo que generó una importante polémica. Según el autor, la resistencia inicial a reconocer los problemas de la norma y la falta de autocrítica perjudicaron especialmente la credibilidad de Montero.
